newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Chirac calls for well in every Third World village.
newsitem.headline: Chirac calls for well in every Third World village.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac, launching an initiative to boost the world's supply of clean water, on Monday called for a well in every Third World village within 10 years.

Water consumption was rising twice as fast as the world's population and 25 million people a year died from polluted water, he said at the opening session of a United Nations conference taking stock of progresss since the 1992 Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro.
"Let's decide together that in 10 years every village in the Third World, and particularly in Africa, should have a well or access to drinking water," he said.
"Let's decide to reduce by a half, in 10 years, the number of urban households which do not have access to drinking water"
He said France planned an international conference on water early next year, bringing together governments, local authorities, international organisations and businesses.
France is keen to seek business abroad for its two giant utilities companies, Generale des Eaux and Lyonnaise des Eaux.

Chirac also called for early action to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and deforestation -- both issues which divided Europe and the United States at a Group of Seven rich nations summit in Denver last weekend.

While Europe is pressing for a 15 percent reduction in greenhouse gases by the year 2010, the United States -- described at the weekend by Chirac as "a huge polluter" -- has resisted such commitments.
Chirac called for agreements on greenhouse gas emissions and forest protection before the end of the year.
"Nobody will be able to repair the ozone layer. Nobody will be able to correct the climatic warming caused by greenhouse gases," he said.
